units.zh: 南齊書卷十九‧志第十一
units.en: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 19 — Treatise 11
units.literal: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 19 — Treatise 11

units.zh: 《木傳》曰：「東方，《易經》地上之木爲《觀》。
units.en: The Wood Treatise says: "In the east, the Book of Changes takes wood on the earth as the hexagram Guan (Viewing).
units.literal: The Wood Treatise says: "To the east, in the Book of Changes, wood upon the earth is the hexagram Guan (Viewing).

units.zh: 故木於人，威儀容貌也。
units.en: Wood, then, stands for a man's dignity and countenance.
units.literal: Thus wood in human affairs signifies bearing and outward appearance.

units.zh: 木者，春生氣之始，農之本也。
units.en: Wood is where spring's life-force begins and the root of farming.
units.literal: Wood is the beginning of spring's generative qi and the foundation of agriculture.

units.zh: 無奪農時，使民歲不過三日，行什一之稅，無貪欲之謀，則木氣從。
units.en: Do not rob the seasons of ploughing; keep yearly corvée to three days or less; take a tenth in tax; plot no greedy schemes — and the wood qi will align.
units.literal: If one does not seize the farming seasons, limits corvée so the people lose no more than three days a year, levies a tithe tax, and harbors no schemes of greed, then the wood qi will follow.

units.zh: 如人君失威儀，逆木行，田獵馳騁，不反宮室，飲食沈湎，不顧禮制，出入無度，多發繇役，以奪民時，作爲姦詐，以奪民財，則木失其性矣。
units.en: But if the ruler casts off dignity, turns against the wood phase, hunts and races without returning to court, drowns in feasting without heed for rites, goes in and out without limit, sends out corvée after corvée to steal the people's seasons, and schemes fraud to steal their goods — then wood loses its true nature.
units.literal: If the ruler loses proper bearing, reverses the wood phase, hunts and gallops without returning to the palace, sinks into drink and food without regard for ritual, comes and goes without measure, levies many corvée duties to seize the people's seasons, and practices deceit to seize the people's wealth, then wood loses its nature.

units.zh: 蓋以工匠之爲輪矢者多傷敗，故曰木不曲直。」
units.en: Craftsmen who shape wheels and arrows often spoil their work; hence the omen that wood will not bend true."
units.literal: It is because artisans making wheels and arrows often produce damaged goods; hence the saying that wood is not straight or bent."

units.zh: 宋泰豫元年，京師祗垣寺皂莢樹枯死。
units.en: In the first year of Song Taiyu, the honey-locust tree at Zhiyuan Temple in the capital withered and died.
units.literal: In the first year of Song Taiyu, the honey-locust tree at Zhiyuan Temple in the capital withered and died.

units.zh: 昇明末，忽更生花葉。
units.en: At the end of Shengming, it suddenly put forth flowers and leaves again.
units.literal: At the end of Shengming, it suddenly again put forth flowers and leaves.

units.zh: 京房易傳曰：「樹枯冬生，不出二年，國喪，君子亡。」
units.en: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "When a tree withers and then grows in winter, within two years there will be mourning in the state and the ruler will perish."
units.literal: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "When a tree withers and then grows in winter, within two years there will be mourning in the state and the ruler will perish."

units.zh: 其占同。
units.en: The omen was the same.
units.literal: Its omen was the same.

units.zh: 宋氏禪位。
units.en: The Song house yielded the throne.
units.literal: The Song house yielded the throne.

units.zh: 建元元年，朱爵𦨵華表柱生枝葉。
units.en: In the first year of Jianyuan, foliage grew on the ornamental pillar at the Vermilion Sparrow Gate.
units.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan, branches and leaves sprouted on the ornamental pillar of the Vermilion Sparrow Gate.

units.zh: 建元初，李子生毛。
units.en: Early in Jianyuan, plum fruit sprouted hairlike growth.
units.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan, plums grew fuzz.

units.zh: 二年，武陵沅頭都尉治有桑樹，方冬生葉。
units.en: In year 2, at the Wuling Yuan-head commandery seat, a mulberry put out leaves in the depth of winter.
units.literal: In year 2, at the headquarters of the Commander of the Head of Yuan in Wuling, a mulberry tree bore leaves in midwinter.

units.zh: 《京房易傳》曰：「木冬生花，天下有喪。」
units.en: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "Wood flowering in winter — mourning falls on the realm."
units.literal: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "When wood blossoms in winter, the realm will mourn."

units.zh: 其占同。
units.en: The reading matched.
units.literal: The omen was the same.

units.zh: 後二年，宮車晏駕。
units.en: Two years on, the imperial carriage came to rest — the emperor died.
units.literal: Two years later, the imperial carriage halted.

units.zh: 四年，巴州城西古樓腳柏柱數百年，忽生花。
units.en: In year 4, a cypress pillar at the base of the ancient tower west of Bazhou, centuries old, burst into bloom.
units.literal: In year 4, a cypress pillar at the foot of the old tower west of Bazhou city, several centuries old, suddenly flowered.

units.zh: 永明六年，石子崗柏木長二尺四寸，廣四寸半，化爲石。
units.en: In Yongming year 6, a cypress on Stonezi Ridge, two feet four inches long and four and a half inches across, turned to stone.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Yongming, a cypress on Stonezi Ridge, two feet four inches long and four and a half inches wide, turned to stone.

units.zh: 時車駕數游幸，應本傳「木失其性」也。
units.en: The throne was constantly on tour — fulfilling this treatise's line that "wood had lost its nature."
units.literal: At the time the imperial carriage made many excursions — matching this treatise's "wood loses its nature."

units.zh: 永明中，大𦨵一舶無故自沈，艚中無水。
units.en: In Yongming, one great warship sank for no apparent reason; the hold held no water.
units.literal: During Yongming, one great war vessel sank without cause; there was no water in the hold.

units.zh: 隆昌元年，廬陵王子卿齋屋梁柱際無故出血。
units.en: In the first year of Longchang, blood seeped without cause from the beam-and-post joint in Prince Ziqing of Luling's fasting hall.
units.literal: In the first year of Longchang, at the junction of beam and column in the fasting hall of Xiao Ziqing, Prince of Luling, blood flowed without cause.

units.zh: 建武初，始安王遙光治廟，截東安寺屋以直廟垣，截梁，水出如淚。
units.en: Early in Jianwu, Prince Yaoguang of Shi'an rebuilt his ancestral shrine, trimming Dong'an Temple's roofline to square the shrine wall; when the beams were cut, water welled up like tears.
units.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu, when Prince of Shi'an Xiao Yaoguang repaired his shrine, he cut off part of Dong'an Temple's building to align the shrine wall; when beams were cut, water flowed like tears.

units.zh: 《貌傳》曰：「失威儀之制，怠慢驕恣，謂之狂，則不肅矣。
units.en: The Appearance Treatise says: "Cast off the rules of dignity, grow slack, proud, and wild — that is called frenzy, and reverence is gone.
units.literal: The Appearance Treatise says: "To lose the regulations of bearing, to be negligent, arrogant, and unrestrained — this is called frenzy, and then there is no solemnity.

units.zh: 下不敬，則上無威。
units.en: When inferiors withhold respect, superiors have no awe.
units.literal: If those below are not reverent, then those above have no authority.

units.zh: 天下旣不敬，又肆其驕恣，肆之則不從。
units.en: When the realm is already disrespectful and then indulges pride and license, indulgence breeds disobedience.
units.literal: When all under Heaven are already irreverent and additionally give free rein to arrogance and license, once they give free rein they will not obey.

units.zh: 夫不敬其君，不從其政，則陰氣勝，故曰厥罰常雨。」
units.en: Fail to honor the ruler and refuse his rule, and yin overcomes — hence the penalty called unending rain."
units.literal: When they do not revere their lord and do not follow his government, yin qi prevails; hence the saying that the corresponding penalty is constant rain."

units.zh: 永明八年四月，己巳起陰雨，晝或暫晴，夜時見星月，連雨積霖，至十七日乃止。
units.en: In Yongming the eighth year, fourth month, from jisi day rain set in; days sometimes briefly cleared, nights sometimes showed stars and moon; the downpour lasted until the seventeenth before it broke.
units.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year of Yongming, from the day jisi onward it rained continuously; by day it sometimes cleared briefly, by night stars and moon sometimes appeared; the rains piled up until the seventeenth when they stopped.

units.zh: 十一年四月辛巳朔，去三月戊寅起，而其間暫時晴，從四月一日又陰雨，晝或見日，夜乍見月，回復陰雨，至七月乃止。
units.en: On the xinsi new moon of the fourth month in year 11 — rain had begun in the third month on wuyin day, with brief clears between — from the first of the fourth month cloud and rain returned; by day the sun sometimes broke through, by night the moon flickered, then rain again, until the seventh month at last ended.
units.literal: On the first day xinsi of the fourth month of year 11, counting from wuyin in the third month, with brief clear intervals in between; from the first of the fourth month rain returned, by day the sun sometimes showed, by night the moon would flash, then rain again, until the seventh month when it stopped.

units.zh: 永泰元年十二月二十九日雨，至永元元年五月二十一日乃晴。
units.en: Rain from the twenty-ninth of the twelfth month, Yongtai year 1, until fair skies on the twenty-first of the fifth month, Yongyuan year 1.
units.literal: Rain from the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth month, first year of Yongtai, until clear weather on the twenty-first day of the fifth month, first year of Yongyuan.

units.zh: 京房占曰：「冬雨，天下饑。
units.en: Jing Fang's prognostication says: "Rain in winter — famine under Heaven.
units.literal: Jing Fang's prognostication says: "Winter rain — famine throughout the realm.

units.zh: 春雨，有小兵。」
units.en: Rain in spring — small wars."
units.literal: Spring rain — minor military disturbances."

units.zh: 時虜寇雍州，餘應本傳。
units.en: Barbarians were raiding Yongzhou — the rest fulfilled this treatise.
units.literal: At the time the barbarians raided Yongzhou; the rest matched this treatise.

units.zh: 《傳》曰：「大雨雪，猶庶征之常雨也，然有甚焉。
units.en: The Treatise says: "Great rain and snow belong among the usual signs of unending rain, yet they mark something worse.
units.literal: The Treatise says: "Heavy rain and snow are still like the ordinary sign of constant rain among the various portents, yet there is something more severe.

units.zh: 雨，陰。
units.en: Rain is yin.
units.literal: Rain is yin.

units.zh: 大雨雪者，陰之畜積甚也。
units.en: Heavy rain and snow mean yin has stockpiled to excess.
units.literal: Heavy rain and snow mean yin's accumulation is excessive.

units.zh: 一曰與大水同象，曰攻爲雪耳。」
units.en: Another reading: it shares the omen of great flood — assault turned into snow."
units.literal: One explanation: it shares the same image as great flood — that is, assault transformed into snow."

units.zh: 建元二年閏月己丑，雨雪。
units.en: In the second year of Jianyuan, intercalary month, jichou day — rain mixed with snow.
units.literal: Intercalary month, year 2 of Jianyuan, day jichou — rain and snow.

units.zh: 三年十一月，雨雪，或陰或晦，八十餘日，至四年二月乃止。
units.en: Eleventh month, year 3 — rain and snow, skies dull or dark, for eighty-odd days until the second month of year 4.
units.literal: Eleventh month, year 3 — rain and snow, sometimes overcast sometimes dim, for more than eighty days until the second month of year 4 when it stopped.

units.zh: 《傳》曰：「雷於天地爲長子，以其首長萬物，與之出入。
units.en: The Treatise says: "Thunder between Heaven and Earth is the eldest son — it goes first among the myriad things in their rising and falling.
units.literal: The Treatise says: "Thunder in Heaven and Earth is the eldest son, because it leads all things at their coming forth and going in.

units.zh: 故雷出萬物出，雷入萬物入。
units.en: Thunder out, the myriad things come out; thunder in, they go in.
units.literal: Thus when thunder emerges all things emerge; when thunder withdraws all things withdraw.

units.zh: 夫雷者，人君之象，入則除害，出則興利。
units.en: Thunder images the ruler: inward it clears harm, outward it brings gain.
units.literal: Thunder is the image of the ruler; when it enters it removes harm, when it emerges it brings benefit.

units.zh: 雷之微氣以正月出，其有聲者以二月出，以八月入，其餘微者以九月入。
units.en: Thunder's faint breath appears in the first month; audible thunder in the second; it withdraws in the eighth; what remains, faintly, in the ninth.
units.literal: Thunder's subtle qi emerges in the first month; that which has sound emerges in the second month; it withdraws in the eighth month; the remaining subtle form withdraws in the ninth month.

units.zh: 冬三月雷無出者；
units.en: Through the three winter months thunder should not sound;
units.literal: In the three winter months thunder does not emerge;

units.zh: 若是陽不閉陰，則出涉危難而害萬物也。」
units.en: but if yang fails to seal yin, it breaks out, trespasses on danger, and harms the myriad things."
units.literal: but if yang does not close off yin, then it emerges, crosses into peril, and harms the myriad things."

units.zh: 建元元年十月壬午，夜電光，因雷鳴。
units.en: In the first year of Jianyuan, tenth month, renwu night — lightning, then thunder.
units.literal: Tenth month, year 1 of Jianyuan, day renwu — at night lightning, then thunder.

units.zh: 十一月庚戌，電光，有頃雷鳴，久而止。
units.en: Eleventh month, gengxu — lightning; thunder followed after a moment and rumbled on before stopping.
units.literal: Eleventh month, gengxu — lightning; after a while thunder; long before it ceased.

units.zh: 永明五年正月戊申，夜西北雷聲。
units.en: Yongming the fifth year, first month, wushen night — thunder in the northwest.
units.literal: Yongming the fifth year, first month, wushen — at night thunder in the northwest.

units.zh: 六年十月甲申，夜陰細雨，始聞雷鳴於西北上。
units.en: In the sixth year, tenth month, jiashen night — a light, steady rain; thunder first rolled from the northwest.
units.literal: In the sixth year, tenth month, jiashen — at night fine drizzling rain; thunder was first heard from the northwest.

units.zh: 七年正月甲子，夜陰，雷鳴西南坤宮，隆隆一聲而止。
units.en: In the seventh year, first month, jiazi night — overcast; thunder in the southwest Kun quarter, a single deep roll and silence.
units.literal: In the seventh year, first month, jiazi — night overcast; thunder in the southwest Kun palace, one rumbling clap and stop.

units.zh: 八年正月庚戌，夜雷起坎宮水門，其音隆隆，一聲而止。
units.en: In the eighth year, first month, gengxu night — thunder at the Kan quarter's water gate, a deep rumble, one stroke and done.
units.literal: In the eighth year, first month, gengxu — at night thunder rose at the Kan palace water gate, sound rumbling, one clap and stop.

units.zh: 九年二月丙子，西北有電光，因聞雷聲隆隆，仍續十聲而止。
units.en: In the ninth year, second month, bingzi — lightning northwest, then rolling thunder, ten strokes in succession before it ceased.
units.literal: In the ninth year, second month, bingzi — lightning in the northwest, then rumbling thunder continuing ten claps before stopping.

units.zh: 十年二月庚戌，夜南方有電光，因聞雷聲隆隆相續，丁亥止。
units.en: In the tenth year, second month, gengxu night — lightning in the south, then rolling thunder one after another until dinghai.
units.literal: In the tenth year, second month, gengxu — at night lightning in the south, then rumbling thunder in succession, stopping at dinghai.

units.zh: 十月庚子，電雷起西北。
units.en: Tenth month, gengzi — lightning and thunder broke out in the northwest.
units.literal: Tenth month, gengzi — lightning and thunder rose in the northwest.

units.zh: 十一月丁丑，西南有光，因聞雷聲隱隱，再聲而止。
units.en: In the eleventh month, on the day dingchou, light appeared in the southwest; then faint thunder rolled twice and fell silent.
units.literal: Eleventh month, dingchou day: light in the southwest; then thunder was heard, faint and low—two rolls, then it stopped.

units.zh: 西南坤宮。
units.en: Southwest—the Kun palace sector.
units.literal: Southwest, the Kun palace.

units.zh: 十二月甲申，陰雨，有電光，因聞西南及西北上雷鳴，頻續三聲。
units.en: In the twelfth month, on the day jiashen, the sky was overcast and rain fell; lightning flashed, and thunder rolled three times from the southwest and from above the northwest.
units.literal: Twelfth month, jiashen day: overcast rain; there was lightning, and thunder was heard from the southwest and from above the northwest—three rolls in succession.

units.zh: 丙申，夜聞西北上雷頻續二聲。
units.en: On the day bingshen, at night thunder rolled twice from above the northwest.
units.literal: Bingshen day: at night thunder was heard from above the northwest, two rolls in succession.

units.zh: 辛亥，雷雨。
units.en: On the day xinhai, thunder and rain.
units.literal: Xinhai day: thunder and rain.

units.zh: 《傳》曰：「雨雹，君臣之象也。
units.en: The Treatise says: "Rain and hail image the ruler and his ministers.
units.literal: The Treatise says: "Rain and hail are the image of ruler and minister.

units.zh: 陽之氣專爲雹，陰之氣專爲霰。
units.en: Yang qi by itself forms hail; yin qi by itself forms graupel.
units.literal: Yang qi alone makes hail; yin qi alone makes graupel.

units.zh: 陽專而陰脅之，陰盛而陽薄之。
units.en: When yang holds sway and yin presses upon it; when yin grows strong and yang is driven thin.
units.literal: When yang dominates and yin constrains it; when yin flourishes and yang is thinned.

units.zh: 雹者，陰薄陽之象也。
units.en: Hail is the sign of yin pressing yang thin.
units.literal: Hail is the image of yin thinning yang.

units.zh: 霰者，陽脅陰之符也。
units.en: Graupel is the token of yang constraining yin.
units.literal: Graupel is the token of yang constraining yin.

units.zh: 《春秋》不書霰者，猶月蝕也。」
units.en: The Spring and Autumn Annals does not record graupel—much as it omits lunar eclipses."
units.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals does not record graupel—like lunar eclipses."

units.zh: 建元四年五月戊午朔，雹。
units.en: In the fourth year of Jianyuan, fifth month, new moon of the day wuwu: hail fell.
units.literal: Jianyuan year 4, fifth month, first day of the month wuwu: hail.

units.zh: 永明元年九月乙丑，雹落大如蒜子，須臾乃止。
units.en: Yongming 1, ninth month, day yichou: hailstones fell as large as garlic cloves, then ceased in a moment.
units.literal: Yongming year 1, ninth month, yichou day: hail fell large as garlic cloves; shortly it stopped.

units.zh: 十一年四月辛亥，雹落大如蒜子，須臾滅。
units.en: In the eleventh year, fourth month, day xinhai: hailstones as large as garlic cloves fell, then vanished in a moment.
units.literal: In the eleventh year, fourth month, xinhai day: hail fell large as garlic cloves; shortly it vanished.

units.zh: 《貌傳》又曰：「上失節而狂，下怠慢而不敬，上下失道，輕法侵制，不顧君上，因以薦饑。
units.en: The Appearance Treatise also says: "When the ruler above loses measure and turns reckless, those below grow negligent and disrespectful; above and below abandon the Way, laws are trifled with and boundaries violated, with no regard for the throne—then famine is offered up.
units.literal: The Appearance Treatise also says: "When the ruler above loses measure and turns reckless, those below are negligent and disrespectful; above and below lose the Way, laws are lightly violated and boundaries encroached upon, heedless of the sovereign—famine follows.

units.zh: 貌氣毀，故有雞禍。」
units.en: When the qi of appearance is ruined, calamities of chickens arise."
units.literal: When appearance qi is ruined, chicken calamities arise."

units.zh: 「一曰水歲雞多死及爲怪，亦是也。
units.en: Another reading: "In a Water year chickens die in great numbers or turn strange—this too applies.
units.literal: Another reading: "In a Water year many chickens die or turn monstrous—this too counts.

units.zh: 上下不相信，大臣姦宄，民爲寇盜，故曰厥極惡。」
units.en: When sovereign and subjects no longer trust one another, ministers breed conspiracy, and the people turn to banditry—hence the reading that the ultimate omen is wickedness."
units.literal: When above and below do not trust each other, great ministers plot treachery, and the people become brigands—hence the saying that the extreme turns wicked."

units.zh: 「一曰民多被刑，或形貌醜惡，風俗狂慢，變節易度，則爲輕剽奇怪之服，故曰時則有服妖。」
units.en: Another reading: "When many of the people suffer punishments, or their looks grow ugly, and customs turn reckless and arrogant, changing norms and altering standards, then frivolous, fierce, strange, and bizarre clothing appears; hence it is said that at such a time there are clothing prodigies."
units.literal: Another reading: "When many of the people suffer punishments, or their forms and appearances are ugly, and customs are reckless and arrogant, changing norms and altering standards, then there will be frivolous, fierce, strange, and bizarre clothing; hence it is said that at such a time there are clothing prodigies."

units.zh: 永明中，宮內服用射獵錦文，爲騎射兵戈之象。
units.en: In Yongming, the palace adopted hunting brocades patterned with bow and lance—emblems of horsemen, archery, and arms.
units.literal: During Yongming, within the palace they wore hunting brocade with archery motifs—an image of mounted shooting and weapons of war.

units.zh: 至建武初，虜大爲寇。
units.en: By the opening of Jianwu, the northern foes raided on a great scale.
units.literal: By the opening of Jianwu, the barbarians raided on a great scale.

units.zh: 永明中，蕭諶開博風帽後裙之制，爲破後帽。
units.en: In Yongming, Xiao Chen introduced broad wind hats with long back skirts—the style called the torn-back hat.
units.literal: During Yongming, Xiao Chen devised broad wind hats with trailing back skirts—the fashion called the torn-back hat.

units.zh: 世祖崩後，諶建廢立，誅滅諸王。
units.en: After Shizu’s death, Chen engineered deposition and enthronement and put the princes to death.
units.literal: After Shizu’s death, Chen engineered deposition and enthronement and executed the princes.

units.zh: 永明末，民閒制倚勸帽。
units.en: At the end of Yongming, the people fashioned leaning-admonition hats.
units.literal: At the end of Yongming, common folk made leaning-admonition hats.

units.zh: 及海陵廢，明帝之立，勸進之事，倚立可待也。
units.en: When Hailing was deposed and Mingdi took the throne—the urging of accession: lean and stand, and the deed was done.
units.literal: When Hailing was deposed and Mingdi enthroned—the matter of urging accession: to lean and stand was all that waited.

units.zh: 建武中，帽裙覆頂；
units.en: In Jianwu, hat skirts were worn over the crown;
units.literal: During Jianwu, hat skirts covered the crown;

units.zh: 東昏時，以爲裠應在下，而今在上，不祥，斷之。
units.en: In Dong Hun’s time they judged it ill-omened that skirts meant to hang below now hung above, and had them cut away.
units.literal: in Dong Hun’s time they held it inauspicious that skirts should lie below but now lay above—inauspicious; they cut them off.

units.zh: 羣下反上之象也。
units.en: An omen of the many rebelling against their superiors.
units.literal: An image of the masses turning against what is above.

units.zh: 永元中，東昏侯自造遊宴之服，綴以花采錦繡，難得詳也。
units.en: In Yongyuan, the Marquis of Dong Hun devised his own garments for feasts and outings, sewn with floral brocade beyond full reckoning.
units.literal: In Yongyuan, the Marquis of Dong Hun himself devised feast and tour garments adorned with floral brocade—too many to detail.

units.zh: 羣小又造四種帽，帽因勢爲名：一曰山鵲歸林者，《詩》云「《鵲巢》，夫人之德」，東昏寵嬖淫亂，故鵲歸其林藪；
units.en: Petty men fashioned four kinds of hat, each named from the drift of events: first, "Magpie of the hills returning to the grove"—the Odes have "Magpie Nest—the wife’s virtue"; Dong Hun doted on favorites and lewd disorder, so the magpie returned to its covert;
units.literal: Petty men also made four kinds of hat, each named by allusion to the times: first, "Magpie of the hills returning to the grove"—the Odes say "Magpie Nest—the wife’s virtue"; Dong Hun favored debauchery, so the magpie returned to its thicket;

units.zh: 二曰「兔子度坑」，天意言天下將有逐兔之事也；
units.en: second, "Rabbit crossing the ditch"—Heaven’s meaning was that the realm would soon know the chase of the hare;
units.literal: second, "Rabbit crossing the ditch"—Heaven’s intent said the realm would soon see a chase-the-rabbit affair;

units.zh: 三曰「反縛黃離嘍」，黃口小鳥也，反縛，面縛之應也；
units.en: third, "Bound yellow fledgling"—the yellow-beaked nestling; reversed binding—the omen of bonds drawn across the face;
units.literal: third, "Bound yellow fledgling"—a yellow-mouth fledgling; binding reversed—the omen of being bound face-forward;

units.zh: 四曰「鳳皇度三橋」，鳳皇者嘉瑞，三橋，梁王宅處也。
units.en: fourth, "Phoenix crossing three bridges"—the phoenix is a blessed omen; the three bridges mark where the Prince of Liang dwelt.
units.literal: fourth, "Phoenix crossing three bridges"—the phoenix is an auspicious sign; three bridges—the seat of the Prince of Liang’s house.

units.zh: 《貌傳》又曰：「危亂端見，則天地之異生。
units.en: The Appearance Treatise also says: "When the first signs of peril appear, Heaven and Earth produce anomalies.
units.literal: The Appearance Treatise also says: "When the portents of peril and disorder appear, anomalies of Heaven and Earth arise.

units.zh: 木者青，故曰青眚，爲惡祥。
units.en: Wood is green; hence the green portent—a baleful sign.
units.literal: Wood is green; hence the green calamity—an evil omen.

units.zh: 凡貌傷者，金沴木，木沴金，衡氣相通。」
units.en: Whenever appearance is wounded, metal injures wood and wood injures metal—the qi of the scales flow into one another."
units.literal: Whenever appearance is injured, metal harms wood and wood harms metal—the balancing qi communicate."

units.zh: 延興元年，海陵王初立，文惠太子冢上有物如人，長數丈，青色，直上天，有聲如雷。
units.en: Yanxing 1, when the Prince of Hailing was first raised to the throne, above Crown Prince Wenhui’s mound a figure like a man, several zhang in height and green in color, rose straight to Heaven with a roar like thunder.
units.literal: Yanxing year 1, when the Prince of Hailing was first enthroned, above Crown Prince Wenhui’s tomb something like a person, several zhang tall and green, shot straight to Heaven with a sound like thunder.

units.zh: 火，南方，揚光輝，出炎𤓀爲明者也。
units.en: Fire belongs to the south; it lifts light and splendor, and from leaping flame comes radiance.
units.literal: Fire is the south; it spreads light and glory, and from flame and blaze emerges brilliance.

units.zh: 人君向明而治，蓋取其象。
units.en: The ruler faces the light in his rule—he takes this for his emblem.
units.literal: The ruler turns toward the light in governing—he takes this as his image.

units.zh: 以知人爲分，讒佞旣遠，羣賢在位，則爲明而火氣從矣。
units.en: He assigns office by men’s gifts; flatterers are kept distant and the worthy stand in post—then he is luminous and fire qi answers.
units.literal: He assigns men by their gifts; slanderers are kept far, worthies hold office—then he is enlightened and fire qi follows.

units.zh: 人君疑惑，棄法律，不誅讒邪，則讒口行，內間骨肉，外疏忠臣，至殺世子，逐功臣，以妾爲妻，則火失其性，上災宗廟，下災府榭，內熯本朝，外熯闕觀，雖興師衆，不能救也。
units.en: When the ruler wavers, casts aside law, and will not punish slander and wickedness—then slander runs free, flesh and bone are divided within and loyal ministers cast off without, until the heir is slain and worthy servants banished, a concubine raised to wife—then fire loses its nature: disaster strikes the ancestral shrines above and the palaces below, flame devours the court within and the gate-towers without; though hosts be mobilized, none can redeem it.
units.literal: When the ruler is doubtful, abandons the laws, and does not punish slander and evil—then slander runs, kin are estranged within and loyal ministers kept afar without, until the heir is killed and meritorious servants driven off, a concubine made wife—then fire loses its nature: calamity above on the ancestral shrines, calamity below on halls and pavilions, burning within the court and burning without the gate towers; even if armies are raised, nothing can save.

units.zh: 永明三年正月，甲夜西北有野火，光上生精。
units.en: Yongming 3, first month, first watch of night: wild fire in the northwest; from its light fire-essence rose.
units.literal: Yongming the third year, first month, jia night: wild fire in the northwest; light above produced essence.

units.zh: 西北有四，東北有一，並長七八尺，黃赤色。
units.en: Four in the northwest and one in the northeast—each seven or eight chi long, yellow and red.
units.literal: Four in the northwest, one in the northeast—all seven or eight chi long, yellow-red in color.

units.zh: 三月庚午，丙夜北面有野火，光上生精，長六尺；
units.en: Third month, day gengwu, third watch of night: wild fire to the north; essence rose from its light, six chi long;
units.literal: Third month, gengwu day, bing night: wild fire to the north; light above produced essence, six chi long;

units.zh: 戊夜又有一枚，長五尺，並黃赤色。
units.en: fifth watch again one, five chi long—all yellow-red.
units.literal: fifth watch again one, five chi long—all yellow-red.

units.zh: 四年正月丁亥，夜有火精三處。
units.en: In the fourth year, first month, day dinghai: at night fire essence appeared in three places.
units.literal: In the fourth year, first month, dinghai day: at night fire essence in three places.

units.zh: 閏月丁巳，夜有火精四所。
units.en: Intercalary month, day dingsi: at night fire essence appeared in four places.
units.literal: Intercalary month, dingsi day: at night fire essence in four places.

units.zh: 十二月辛酉，夜東南有野火精二枚。
units.en: Twelfth month, day xinyou: at night two wild fire essences in the southeast.
units.literal: Twelfth month, xinyou day: at night two wild fire essences in the southeast.

units.zh: 五年十二月丙寅，夜西北有野火，火上生精，一枚，長三尺，黃白色。
units.en: In the fifth year, twelfth month, day bingyin: at night wild fire in the northwest; essence rose from the flame, one piece three chi long, yellow-white.
units.literal: In the fifth year, twelfth month, bingyin day: at night wild fire in the northwest; essence on the fire, one piece three chi long, yellow-white.

units.zh: 六年十一月戊申，夜西南及北三面有野火，火生精，九枚，竝長二尺，黃赤色。
units.en: In the sixth year, eleventh month, day wushen: at night wild fire burned in the southwest and on three sides to the north; the flames bore essence, nine in all, each two chi long and yellow-red.
units.literal: In the sixth year, eleventh month, wushen day: at night wild fire on the southwest and on three sides to the north; fire produced essence, nine pieces, all two chi long, yellow-red.

units.zh: 九年二月丙寅，甲夜北面有野火，火上生精，二枚，西北又一枚，並長三尺，須臾消。
units.en: In the ninth year, second month, bingyin day: on the jia watch, wild fire burned in the north; spirit-forms rose from the flames—two together, and a third in the northwest—each three chi tall; in a breath they were gone.
units.literal: In the ninth year, second month, day bingyin; on the jia night watch, in the north there was wild fire; atop the flames spirit-forms arose—two of them, and another in the northwest; each three chi long; in a moment they vanished.

units.zh: 永元二年八月，宮內火，燒西齋璿儀殿及昭陽、顯陽等殿，北至華林牆，西及秘閣，凡屋三千餘間。
units.en: Yongyuan the second year, eighth month: palace fire consumed the Xuanyi Hall in the west quarters, the Zhaoyang and Xianyang halls, and more—north to the Hualin wall, west to the archives—over three thousand rooms in all.
units.literal: In the eighth month of Yongyuan year 2, fire broke out within the palace; it burned the Xuanyi Hall in the west quarters and the Zhaoyang, Xianyang, and other halls, north to the Hualin Park wall and west to the Secretariat archives—more than three thousand rooms in all.

units.zh: 《京房易傳》曰：「君不思道，厥妖火燒宮。」
units.en: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "When the ruler turns from the Way, the omen is fire in the palace."
units.literal: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "When the ruler does not reflect on the Way, the portent is fire burning the palace."

units.zh: 秘閣與《春秋》宣榭火同，天意若曰，旣無紀綱，何用典文爲也！
units.en: The archives blaze matched the Xuan she fire in the Spring and Autumn Annals—as if Heaven said: with no order left in the realm, of what use are the classics?
units.literal: The burning of the archives matches the Xuan she fire in the Spring and Autumn Annals; Heaven's intent seemed to say: since there is no discipline, what use are canonical texts!

units.zh: 二年冬，京師民間相驚云，當行火災，南岸人家往往於籬間得布火纏者，云公家以此禳之。
units.en: That winter, rumor swept the capital that a great fire was due; on the south bank families kept finding cloth-wrapped fire bundles in their hedges—said to be the court's way of warding the calamity off.
units.literal: That winter in year 2, among the people of the capital there was mutual alarm, saying a fire disaster was coming; households on the south bank often found cloth-wrapped fire bundles in their fences, saying the authorities used these to avert it.

units.zh: 三年正月，豫章郡天火燒三千餘家。
units.en: In the third year, first month: heaven fire in Yuzhang commandery burned more than three thousand homes.
units.literal: In the first month of year 3, heaven fire in Yuzhang commandery burned more than three thousand households.

units.zh: 京房《易》占曰：「天火下燒民屋，是謂亂治殺兵作。」
units.en: Jing Fang's Changes divination says: "Heaven fire that falls and burns commoners' houses means rule in chaos and armies raised for slaughter."
units.literal: Jing Fang's Changes divination says: "When heaven fire descends to burn the people's houses, this is called disorder in governance and the rising of troops for killing."

units.zh: 是年，臺軍與義師偏衆相攻於南江諸郡。
units.en: That year court armies and righteous-army factions clashed across the southern river commanderies.
units.literal: That year, court troops and partisan bands of the righteous armies fought one another in the southern river commanderies.

units.zh: 三年二月，乾和殿西廂火，燒屋三十間。
units.en: In the third year, second month: fire in the west wing of Qianhe Hall destroyed thirty rooms.
units.literal: In the second month of year 3, fire in the west wing of Qianhe Hall burned thirty rooms.

units.zh: 是時西齋旣火，帝徙居東齋，高宗所住殿也。
units.en: The west quarters having already burned, the emperor moved to the east quarters—the hall where Emperor Gaozong had lived.
units.literal: At that time the west quarters had already burned; the emperor moved to the east quarters—the hall where Emperor Gaozong had dwelt.

units.zh: 與燒宮占同。
units.en: The same reading as for a burning palace.
units.literal: The same as the omen for burning the palace.

units.zh: 《傳》又曰：「犯上者不誅，則草犯霜而不死。
units.en: The Treatise also says: "If those who rise against their betters go unpunished, grass will meet frost and not die.
units.literal: The Treatise also says: "When those who offend superiors are not executed, then grass meets frost yet does not die.

units.zh: 或殺不以時，事在殺生失柄，故曰草妖也。」
units.en: Or killing out of season—the fault is slaughter without mastery; hence the omen of grass."
units.literal: Or killing not at the proper season—the matter lies in taking life and losing control; hence it is called a grass portent."

units.zh: 一曰：「草妖者，失衆之象也。」
units.en: Another text says: "Grass portents show the ruler has lost the people."
units.literal: Another version says: "Grass portents are an image of losing the multitude."

units.zh: 永元中，御刀黃文濟家齋前種昌蒲，忽生花，光影照壁，成五采，其兒見之，餘人不見也。
units.en: In Yongyuan, Huang Wenji of the Imperial Blades had calamus before his study suddenly bloom; colored light played on the wall; only his child saw it—the rest did not.
units.literal: During Yongyuan, Huang Wenji of the Imperial Blades—calamus planted before his study suddenly flowered; light and shadow shone on the wall in five colors; his child saw it, the others did not.

units.zh: 少時，文濟被殺。
units.en: Soon after, Wenji was put to death.
units.literal: Before long, Wenji was killed.

units.zh: 劉歆《視傳》有羽蟲之孽，謂雞禍也。
units.en: Liu Xin's Treatise on Appearances lists portents among feathered creatures—the calamity of the chicken.
units.literal: Liu Xin's Treatise on Appearances has portents of feathered creatures, called the calamity of chickens.

units.zh: 班固案《易》雞屬《巽》，今以羽蟲之孽類是也，依歆說附《視傳》云。
units.en: Ban Gu notes that in the Changes the chicken belongs to Xun, Wind; feathered portents are classed likewise. Following Liu Xin, appended to the Treatise on Appearances:
units.literal: Ban Gu notes that in the Changes the chicken belongs to Xun (Wind); now classifying feathered-creature portents accordingly, following Liu Xin's explanation appended to the Treatise on Appearances it says:

units.zh: 建武二年，有大鳥集建安，形如水犢子。
units.en: Jianwu year 2: a great bird settled at Jian'an, shaped like a water-buffalo calf.
units.literal: In Jianwu year 2, a great bird gathered at Jian'an, shaped like a water-buffalo calf.

units.zh: 其年，郡大水。
units.en: That year the commandery was struck by flood.
units.literal: That year, the commandery suffered a great flood.

units.zh: 三年，大鳥集東陽郡，太守沈約表云：「鳥身備五采，赤色居多。」
units.en: Year 3: a great bird gathered in Dongyang; Administrator Shen Yue reported: "Its body showed all five colors, red predominating."
units.literal: In year 3, a great bird gathered in Dongyang commandery; Administrator Shen Yue memorialized: "The bird's body bore all five colors, mostly red."

units.zh: 案《樂緯葉圖徵》云：「焦明鳥質赤，至則水之感也。」
units.en: The Music Weft's Leaf Diagram Prognostications says: "The Jiaoming bird is red in substance; its coming is water's omen."
units.literal: Examining the Music Weft's Leaf Diagram Prognostications: "The Jiaoming bird's substance is red; when it arrives it is the sensation of water."

units.zh: 永明二年四月，烏巢內殿東鴟尾。
units.en: Yongming the second year, fourth month: crows nested on the inner palace's eastern chiwen finial.
units.literal: In the fourth month of Yongming year 2, crows nested on the eastern chiwen finial of the inner palace.

units.zh: 三年，大鳥集會稽上虞。
units.en: Year 3: a great bird gathered at Shangyu in Kuaiji.
units.literal: In year 3, a great bird gathered at Shangyu in Kuaiji.

units.zh: 其年，縣大水。
units.en: That year the county was flooded.
units.literal: That year, the county suffered a great flood.

units.zh: 《傳》曰：「維水沴火。」
units.en: The Treatise says: "Water injures fire."
units.literal: The Treatise says: "Water harms fire."

units.zh: 又曰：「赤眚赤祥。」
units.en: It also says: "Red portent, red omen."
units.literal: It also says: "Red calamity, red auspice."

units.zh: 建武四年，王晏子德元所居帷屏，無故有血灑之，少日而散。
units.en: Jianwu year 4: at the screens in the home of Wang Yan's son Deyuan, blood appeared from nowhere and faded within days.
units.literal: In Jianwu year 4, at the curtain screens of the residence of Wang Yan's son Deyuan, blood was splashed without cause; in a few days it dispersed.

units.zh: 晏尋被誅。
units.en: Soon after, Yan was executed.
units.literal: Before long Yan was executed.

units.zh: 《思心傳》曰：「心者，土之象也。
units.en: The Traditions on the Mind says: "The mind images earth.
units.literal: The Traditions on the Mind says: "The mind is the image of earth.

units.zh: 思心不睿，其過在瞀亂失紀。
units.en: When the mind is not clear, the fault is confusion and the collapse of rule.
units.literal: When the mind is not perspicacious, the fault lies in muddled disorder and loss of order.

units.zh: 風於陽則爲君，於陰則爲大臣之象，專恣而氣盛，故罰常風。
units.en: Wind in yang stands for the ruler, in yin for great ministers—willfulness and surging breath bring the penalty of unending wind.
units.literal: Wind in yang is the ruler; in yin it is the image of great ministers—when one is willful and qi flourishes, the penalty is constant wind.

units.zh: 心爲五事主，猶土爲五行主也。」
units.en: The mind governs the five duties as earth governs the five phases."
units.literal: The mind is lord of the five affairs, just as earth is lord of the five phases."

units.zh: 一曰：「陰陽相薄，偏氣陽多爲風，其甚也常風。
units.en: Another reading: "Yin and yang clash; where breath leans yang, wind rises—at the extreme, wind without end.
units.literal: Another version: "When yin and yang press against each other, if partial qi is mostly yang it becomes wind; at its extreme, constant wind.

units.zh: 陰氣多者，陰而不雨，其甚也常陰。」
units.en: Where yin abounds, cloud without rain—at the extreme, yin without end."
units.literal: When yin qi is abundant, yin without rain; at its extreme, constant yin."

units.zh: 一曰：「風宵起而晝晦，以應常陰同象也。」
units.en: Another reading: "Wind by night and dimness by day share the omen of unending yin."
units.literal: Another version: "Wind rising at night while day is dim—to correspond to constant yin is the same image."

units.zh: 建元元年十一月庚戌，風夜暴起，雲雷合冥，從戌亥上來。
units.en: In the first year of Jianyuan, eleventh month, gengxu day: at night wind burst up; cloud and thunder shut out the sky; it came from the northwest along the xu-hai quarter.
units.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Jianyuan, day gengxu—wind rose violently at night; clouds and thunder merged into darkness; it came from the northwest (xu-hai).

units.zh: 四年十一月甲寅，酉時風起小駃，至二更雪落，風轉浪津。
units.en: In the fourth year, eleventh month, jiayin: at you hour a light wind rose; at the second watch snow fell and the wind became a tide-surge gale.
units.literal: In the fourth year, eleventh month, jiayin—at you hour wind arose mildly; at the second watch snow fell; wind turned to tide-surge gale.

units.zh: 永明四年二月丙寅，巳時風迅急。
units.en: Yongming the fourth year, second month, bingyin day: at si hour the wind blew hard and fast.
units.literal: In the second month of Yongming year 4, day bingyin—at si hour the wind was swift and urgent.

units.zh: 十一月己丑，戌時風迅急，從西北戌亥上來。
units.en: Eleventh month, jichou day: at xu hour a fierce wind came from the northwest along xu-hai.
units.literal: Eleventh month, jichou—at xu hour wind was swift and urgent, coming from the northwest along xu-hai.

units.zh: 五年五月乙酉，子時風迅急，從西北戌亥上來。
units.en: In the fifth year, fifth month, yiyou day: at zi hour a fierce wind came from the northwest along xu-hai.
units.literal: In the fifth year, fifth month, yiyou—at zi hour wind was swift and urgent, coming from the northwest along xu-hai.

units.zh: 七年正月丁卯，陽徵陰賊之日，時加子，風起迅急，從北方子丑上來，暴疾浪津，寅時止。
units.en: In the seventh year, first month, dingmao—a yang-zhi, yin-thief day, zi hour: wind rose hard from the north along zi-chou, a violent tide-surge gale; it ceased at yin hour.
units.literal: In the seventh year, first month, dingmao—a day of yang zhi and yin thief, hour at zi—wind rose swift and urgent from the north along zi-chou, violent tide-surge gale; it stopped at yin hour.

units.zh: 八年六月乙酉，時加子，風起迅急，暴疾浪津，發屋折木，塵沙，從西南未上來，因雷雨，須臾，風微雨止。
units.en: In the eighth year, sixth month, yiyou day, zi hour: wind rose hard—a violent tide-surge gale that stripped roofs and snapped trees, dust and sand from the southwest along wei; thunder and rain followed; presently the wind fell and the rain stopped.
units.literal: In the eighth year, sixth month, yiyou, hour at zi—wind rose swift and urgent, violent tide-surge gale, tore off roofs and broke trees, dust and sand, from the southwest along wei; then thunder and rain; in a moment wind eased and rain ceased.

units.zh: 九年七月甲寅，陽羽廉貞之日，時加亥，風起迅急，從東方來，暴疾彭勃浪津，至乙卯陰賊時漸微，名羽動羽。
units.en: In the ninth year, seventh month, jiayin—a yang-yu, lianzhen day, hai hour: wind rose hard from the east, a violent surging tide-surge gale; by yimao, yin-thief hour, it slowly died—named "yu stirring yu."
units.literal: In the ninth year, seventh month, jiayin—a day of yang yu and lianzhen, hour at hai—wind rose swift and urgent from the east, violent surging tide-surge gale; by yimao yin-thief hour it gradually faded—called "yu stirring yu."

units.zh: 九月乙丑，時加未，雷，驟雨，風起迅急，暴疾浪津，從西北戌上來。
units.en: Ninth month, yichou day, wei hour: thunder and a downpour; wind rose hard—a violent tide-surge gale from the northwest along xu.
units.literal: Ninth month, yichou, hour at wei—thunder, sudden rain, wind rose swift and urgent, violent tide-surge gale from the northwest along xu.

units.zh: 十月壬辰，陽羽姦邪之日，時加丑，風起從北方子丑上來，暴疾浪津，迅急，塵埃，五日寅時漸微，名羽動宮。
units.en: Tenth month, renchen—a yang-yu, jianxie day, chou hour: wind from the north along zi-chou, a violent tide-surge gale, swift and dusty; on the fifth day at yin hour it slowly died—named "yu stirring gong."
units.literal: Tenth month, renchen—a day of yang yu and jianxie, hour at chou—wind rose from the north along zi-chou, violent tide-surge gale, swift, dust; on the fifth day at yin hour it gradually faded—called "yu stirring gong."

units.zh: 十年正月辛巳，陽商寬大之日，時加寅，風從西北上來，暴疾浪津，迅急，揚沙折木，酉時止。
units.en: In the tenth year, first month, xinsi—a yang-shang, kuanda day, yin hour: wind from the northwest, a violent tide-surge gale, swift, lifting sand and breaking trees; it ceased at you hour.
units.literal: In the tenth year, first month, xinsi—a day of yang shang and kuanda, hour at yin—wind from the northwest, violent tide-surge gale, swift, raised sand and broke trees; stopped at you hour.

units.zh: 二月甲辰，陽徵姦邪之日，時加辰，風起迅急，從西北亥上來，暴疾彭勃浪津，至酉時止。
units.en: Second month, jiachen—a yang-zhi, jianxie day, chen hour: wind rose hard from the northwest along hai, a violent surging tide-surge gale; it ceased at you hour.
units.literal: Second month, jiachen—a day of yang zhi and jianxie, hour at chen—wind rose swift and urgent from the northwest along hai, violent surging tide-surge gale; stopped at you hour.

units.zh: 三月丁酉，陽徵廉貞之日，時加未，風從北方子丑上來，迅急，暴疾浪津，戌時止。
units.en: Third month, dingyou—a yang-zhi, lianzhen day, wei hour: wind from the north along zi-chou, swift and violent as a tide-surge gale; it ceased at xu hour.
units.literal: Third month, dingyou—a day of yang zhi and lianzhen, hour at wei—wind from the north along zi-chou, swift, violent tide-surge gale; stopped at xu hour.

units.zh: 七月庚申，陰角貪狼之日，時加午，風從東北丑上來，迅急浪津，至辛酉巳時漸微。
units.en: Seventh month, gengshen—a yin-jue, tanlang day, wu hour: wind from the northeast along chou, a swift tide-surge gale; by xinyou si hour it slowly died.
units.literal: Seventh month, gengshen—a day of yin jue and tanlang, hour at wu—wind from the northeast along chou, swift tide-surge gale; by xinyou si hour it gradually faded.

units.zh: 十一年二月庚寅，陽角廉貞之日，時加亥，風從西北亥上來，迅疾浪津，丑時漸微，爲角動角。
units.en: Eleventh year, second month, gengyin: on a yang-jue Integrity day, at the hai hour, wind rose from the northwest at hai in a fierce surging billow-gale, easing by chou; the omen was named jue stirring jue.
units.literal: In the eleventh year, second month, gengyin — a yang-jue Integrity day, the hour at hai; wind came from the northwest at hai, fierce surging billow-wind, gradually abating by the chou hour; called jue stirring jue.

units.zh: 七月甲寅，陽羽廉貞之日，時加巳，風從東北寅上來，迅疾浪津，發屋折木，戊夜漸微，爲羽動徵。
units.en: Seventh month, jiayin: on a yang-yu Integrity day, at si hour, wind from the northeast at yin drove a surging billow-gale that stripped roofs and broke trees; it faded in the deep watches of the night — yu stirring zhi.
units.literal: Seventh month, jiayin — a yang-yu Integrity day, the hour at si; wind came from the northeast at yin, fierce surging billow-wind, tearing off roofs and snapping trees; by deep night it gradually abated; called yu stirring zhi.

units.zh: 己巳，陽角寬大之日，時加未，風從戌上來，暴疾，良久止，爲角動商及宮。
units.en: On jisi, a yang-jue Magnanimity day at wei hour, wind burst from xu, violent and sudden, and raged a long while before it ceased — jue stirring shang and gong.
units.literal: Jisi — a yang-jue Magnanimity day, the hour at wei; wind came from xu, violent and sudden; long before it stopped; called jue stirring shang and gong.

units.zh: 凡時無專恣，疑是陰陽相薄。
units.en: Taken together, when no season held exclusive sway, the reading was yin and yang clashing.
units.literal: In general, when the seasons showed no exclusive excess, it was suspected to be yin and yang in conflict.

units.zh: 建武元年三月乙酉，未時風起，浪津暴急，從北方上來，應本傳瞀亂。
units.en: Jianwu 1, third month, yiyou: at wei hour wind rose from the north, a violent surging billow-gale — fulfilling this treatise's omen of muddled rule and lost order.
units.literal: Jianwu year 1, third month, yiyou — at wei hour wind rose, surging billow-wind violent and sudden, from the north, matching this treatise's confusion and disorder.

units.zh: 建武二年、三年、四年，每秋七月、八月，輒大風，三吳尤甚，髮屋折木，殺人。
units.en: In Jianwu 2, 3, and 4 every autumn's seventh and eighth months brought great winds; the Three Wu suffered most — roofs torn away, trees shattered, people killed.
units.literal: Jianwu years 2, 3, and 4 — each autumn in the seventh and eighth months there were great winds; the Three Wu regions suffered worst, stripping roofs, snapping trees, and killing people.

units.zh: 京房占：「獄吏暴，風害人。」
units.en: Jing Fang's reading: "When jailers turn savage, wind becomes a scourge upon the people."
units.literal: Jing Fang's reading: "When prison clerks are cruel, wind harms the people."

units.zh: 時帝嚴刻。
units.en: The throne was pitiless.
units.literal: At the time the emperor was harsh.

units.zh: 永元元年七月十二日，大風，京師十圍樹及官府居民屋皆拔倒，應本傳。
units.en: Yongyuan 1, seventh month, day twelve: a great wind uprooted every tree ten arm-spans around in the capital, government halls and private houses alike — as this treatise foretold.
units.literal: Yongyuan year 1, seventh month, twelfth day — great wind; in the capital, trees ten arm-spans around and the dwellings of offices and commoners were all uprooted — matching this treatise.

units.zh: 《傳》又曰：「山之於地，君之象也。
units.en: The Treatise also says: "A mountain on the earth images the ruler.
units.literal: The Treatise also says: "Mountain to earth is the image of the ruler.

units.zh: 山崩者，君權損，京陵易處，世將變也。
units.en: When mountains fall, royal power wanes, the dynastic tombs must shift, and the age is turning.
units.literal: When mountains collapse, the ruler's authority is diminished, capital tombs change place, and the age is about to turn.

units.zh: 陵轉爲澤，貴將爲賤也。」
units.en: Tombs sink into marsh; the high-born sink low."
units.literal: A mausoleum mound turns into a marsh; the noble will become base."

units.zh: 建元二年夏，廬陵石陽縣長溪水沖激山麓崩，長六七丈，下得柱千餘口，皆十圍，長者一丈，短者八九尺，頭題有古文字，不可識。
units.en: In the second year of Jianyuan, summer: in Shiyang, Luling, the Chang stream scoured the mountain foot until six or seven zhang fell away; beneath lay a thousand-odd pillars, each ten arm-spans thick, from one zhang down to eight or nine chi, their heads carved with ancient script no one could read.
units.literal: the second year of Jianyuan, summer — at Shiyang county in Luling the Chang stream undercut the mountain foot and it collapsed six or seven zhang; below came more than a thousand pillar-sections, all ten arm-spans around, the longest one zhang and the shortest eight or nine chi; the capitals bore ancient characters that could not be read.

units.zh: 江淹以問王儉，儉云：「江東不閑隸書，此秦漢時柱也。」
units.en: Jiang Yan consulted Wang Jian, who said: "East of the Yangtze they no longer read clerical script — these are Qin-Han pillars."
units.literal: Jiang Yan asked Wang Jian; Jian said: "East of the River does not use clerical script; these are pillars from Qin and Han times."

units.zh: 後年宮車晏駕，世變之象也。
units.en: In a later year, the emperor died — an omen that the world was changing.
units.literal: In a later year, the imperial carriage came to rest — a sign that the age was changing.

units.zh: 永明二年秋，始興曲江縣山崩，壅底溪水成陂。
units.en: Yongming 2, autumn: a mountain fell in Qujiang, Shixing, and blocked the stream at its foot into a lake.
units.literal: Yongming year 2, autumn — at Qujiang county in Shixing a mountain collapsed and dammed the stream at its foot into a reservoir.

units.zh: 京房占：「山崩，人主惡之。」
units.en: Jing Fang's reading: "Mountain collapse bodes ill for the sovereign."
units.literal: Jing Fang's reading: "When mountains collapse, the ruler is ill-omened."

units.zh: 《傳》又曰：「雷電所擊，蓋所感也。
units.en: The Treatise also says: "Thunder and lightning strike where they have been provoked.
units.literal: The Treatise also says: "What thunder and lightning strike is what they have moved.

units.zh: 皆思心有尤之所致也。」
units.en: All such blows spring from failings of mind and heart."
units.literal: All are brought on by faults in mind and heart."

units.zh: 建元二年閏六月丙戌，戊夜震電。
units.en: In the second year of Jianyuan, intercalary sixth month, bingxu: thunder and lightning in the fifth watch of the night.
units.literal: the second year of Jianyuan, intercalary sixth month, bingxu — at the wuye watch, thunder and lightning.

units.zh: 四年五月五日，雷雹暗都，雷震于樂游安昌殿，電火焚蕩盡。
units.en: In the fourth year, fifth month, fifth day: thunder and hail plunged the capital into gloom; lightning hit the Anchang Hall in the Music Stroll quarter and fire from the bolt consumed it utterly.
units.literal: In the fourth year, fifth month, fifth day — thunder and hail darkened the capital; thunder struck the Anchang Hall in the Music Stroll quarter, and electric fire burned everything away.

units.zh: 永明八年四月六日，雷震會稽山陰恒山保林寺，刹上四破，電火燒塔，下佛面窗戶不異也。
units.en: Yongming 8, fourth month, day six: lightning struck Baolin Temple on Mount Heng in Shanyin, Kuaiji — the stupa split four ways and fire from the bolt charred the tower, but the Buddha's face and the windows beneath were untouched.
units.literal: Yongming the eighth year, fourth month, sixth day — thunder struck Baolin Temple on Heng Mountain in Shanyin, Kuaiji; the stupa broke in four places; electric fire burned the pagoda, yet the Buddha's face and the window frames below were unchanged.

units.zh: 永明中，雷震東宮南門，無所傷毀，殺食官一人。
units.en: In Yongming, lightning hit the Eastern Palace's south gate without harming the buildings, yet killed one commissary officer.
units.literal: During Yongming, thunder struck the south gate of the Eastern Palace; nothing was damaged or destroyed, but it killed one food-service official.

units.zh: 十一年三月，震于東齋，棟崩。
units.en: In the eleventh year, third month: lightning at the East Studio; the main beam gave way.
units.literal: In the eleventh year, third month — thunder at the East Studio; the ridge-beam collapsed.

units.zh: 左右密欲治繕，竟陵王子良曰：「此豈可治！
units.en: His close attendants quietly proposed repairs; Prince Zi Liang of Jingling said: "This is not something to mend!
units.literal: Attendants in secret wished to repair it; Prince of Jingling Zi Liang said: "How can this be repaired!

units.zh: 留之志吾過，且旌天之愛我也。」
units.en: Leave it as a record of my faults — and a sign that Heaven still favors me."
units.literal: Leave it to record my fault, and to show that Heaven cherishes me."

units.zh: 明年，子良薨。
units.en: The year after, Zi Liang died.
units.literal: The next year Zi Liang died.

units.zh: 《傳》又曰：「土氣亂者，木金水火亂之。」
units.en: The Treatise also says: "When earth's breath falls into chaos, wood, metal, water, and fire throw it into chaos."
units.literal: The Treatise also says: "When earth qi is in disorder, wood, metal, water, and fire disorder it."

units.zh: 建武二年二月丁巳，地震。
units.en: Jianwu 2, second month, dingsi: the earth quaked.
units.literal: Jianwu year 2, second month, dingsi — an earthquake.

units.zh: 永元元年七月，地日夜十八震。
units.en: Yongyuan 1, seventh month: eighteen shocks between dusk and dawn.
units.literal: Yongyuan year 1, seventh month — day and night, eighteen tremors.

units.zh: 九月十九日，地五震。
units.en: Ninth month, day nineteen: five tremors.
units.literal: Nineteenth day of the ninth month — five tremors.

units.zh: 金者，西方，萬物旣成，殺氣之始也。
units.en: Metal belongs to the west: when the ten thousand things are complete, it is where the breath of slaughter begins.
units.literal: Metal is the west; when the myriad things are already formed, it is the beginning of killing qi.

units.zh: 其于王事，兵戎戰伐之道也。
units.en: In the business of kings it is the path of armies, war, and punitive expeditions.
units.literal: In royal affairs it is the way of arms, war, and campaigning.

units.zh: 王者興師動衆，建立旗鼓，仗旄把鉞，以誅殘賊，止暴亂，殺伐應義，則金氣從。
units.en: When a king marshals hosts, plants flags and drums, takes the yak-tail pennon and battle-axe to cut down the cruel and quell riot, and killing answers to justice, metal's breath aligns with him.
units.literal: When the king raises troops and masses forces, sets up banners and drums, bears the yak-tail standard and grasps the battle-axe to execute cruel villains and stop violent disorder, and the slaughter answers to righteousness, then metal qi follows.

units.zh: 工冶鑄化，革形成器也。
units.en: Craftsmen smelt and cast; leather and hide become tools.
units.literal: Artisans smelt and cast, shaping hide into vessels.

units.zh: 人君樂侵陵，好攻戰，貪城邑，輕百姓之命，人民不安，內外騷動，則金失其性。
units.en: But when a ruler revels in seizing what is not his, thirsts for battle, grasps at walled towns, and treats common lives as nothing — the people uneasy, turmoil within and without — metal loses its true nature.
units.literal: When the ruler delights in encroachment, loves attack and war, covets cities and towns, and holds the people's lives cheap, so that the folk are unsettled and turmoil rises within and without, then metal loses its nature.

units.zh: 蓋冶鑄不化，冰滯固堅，故曰金不從革，又曰維木沴金。
units.en: Furnaces fail to transform; ice sets hard and will not yield — hence the omen that metal refuses to be worked, and that wood overwhelms metal.
units.literal: Smelting and casting will not transform; ice congeals and hardens — hence the saying that metal will not obey the work of reform, and again that wood harms metal.

units.zh: 建武四年，明帝出舊宮送豫章王第二女綏安主降嬪，還上輦，輦上金翅無故自折落地。
units.en: Jianwu 4: Emperor Ming left the old palace to send off Princess Sui'an, second daughter of the Prince of Yuzhang, married down as a consort; as he climbed back into the imperial carriage, the golden wing ornaments snapped off without cause and dropped to the ground.
units.literal: Jianwu year 4 — the Ming Emperor left the old palace to escort the second daughter of the Prince of Yuzhang, Princess Sui'an, down in marriage as a consort; returning to mount the imperial carriage, the golden finials on the carriage broke off for no reason and fell to the ground.

units.zh: 《言傳》曰：「言《易》之道，西方曰《兌》，爲口。
units.en: The Speech Treatise says: "In the Changes, the west is Dui — the mouth.
units.literal: The Speech Treatise says: "The Way of the Changes — to the west is Dui, the mouth.

units.zh: 人君過差無度，刑法不一，斂從其重，或有師旅，炕陽之節，若動衆勞民，是言不從。
units.en: When a ruler's excess has no measure, law is inconsistent, taxes take the heavier rate, or armies march in a season of blazing yang — if he stirs hosts and exhausts the people, speech does not follow.
units.literal: When the ruler's excess knows no bound, punishments are not uniform, levies follow the heavier rate, or there are armies on campaign in a season of scorching yang — if he moves the hosts and wears out the people, that is speech not following.

units.zh: 人君旣失衆，政令不從，孤陽持治，下畏君之重刑，陽氣勝則旱象至，故曰厥罰常陽也。」
units.en: Once the ruler has lost the people and edicts go unheeded, a lone yang clings to power; inferiors dread his heavy punishments; yang overcomes and drought follows — hence the penalty called unending yang."
units.literal: When the ruler has already lost the people and commands are not obeyed, a solitary yang holds governance; those below fear the ruler's heavy punishments; when yang qi prevails the sign of drought arrives — hence the penalty called constant yang."

units.zh: 建元三年，大旱，時有虜寇。
units.en: the third year of Jianyuan: severe drought; barbarians were raiding.
units.literal: the third year of Jianyuan — great drought; at the time there were barbarian raiders.

units.zh: 永民三年，大旱，明年，唐㝢之起。
units.en: Yongming 3: severe drought; the year after, Tang Yu rebelled.
units.literal: Yongming year 3 — great drought; the next year Tang Yu rose in revolt.

units.zh: 建武二年，大旱，時虜寇方盛，皆動衆之應也。
units.en: Jianwu 2: severe drought while barbarian raids were at their peak — in each case the omen answered to armies on the march.
units.literal: Jianwu year 2 — great drought; at the time barbarian raiders were at their height; all were responses to moving the hosts.

units.zh: 《言傳》曰：「下旣悲苦君上之行，又畏嚴刑而不敢正言，則必先發於歌謠。
units.en: The Speech Treatise says: "When the people grieve at their lord's ways yet fear his harsh law and dare not speak straight, the grievance surfaces first in songs.
units.literal: The Speech Treatise says: "When those below both grieve at the ruler's conduct and fear harsh punishments yet dare not speak plainly, it must first break out in ballads.

units.zh: 歌謠，口事也。
units.en: Ballads are the work of the mouth.
units.literal: Ballads are the business of the mouth.

units.zh: 口氣逆則惡言，或有怪謠焉。」
units.en: When breath in the mouth turns awry, vicious words appear — or uncanny rhymes."
units.literal: When breath in the mouth turns contrary there is evil speech, or strange ballads."

units.zh: 宋泰始旣失彭城，江南始傳種消梨，先時所無，百姓爭欲種植。
units.en: After the Song lost Pengcheng in the Taishi era, south of the Yangtze a new pear called the melt-away pear — unknown before — spread from hand to hand, and everyone rushed to plant it.
units.literal: After Song lost Pengcheng in the Taishi era, south of the Yangtze people first passed around planting the melt-away pear, which had not existed before; commoners vied to plant it.

units.zh: 識者曰：「當有姓蕭而來者。」
units.en: Readers of portents said: "Someone of the Xiao clan is coming."
units.literal: Those who read omens said: "One of the Xiao surname will come."

units.zh: 十餘年，齊受禪。
units.en: A dozen years later Qi took the Mandate.
units.literal: After ten-odd years Qi received the Mandate.

units.zh: 元徽中，童謠曰：「襄陽白銅蹄，郎殺荊州兒。」
units.en: In the Yuanhui years, children sang: "White bronze hooves at Xiangyang—the young lord will slay Jingzhou's heir."
units.literal: In the Yuanhui era, a children's rhyme ran: "Xiangyang's white bronze hooves—the lad will kill Jingzhou's son."

units.zh: 後沈攸之反，雍州刺史張敬兒襲江陵，殺沈攸之子元琰等。
units.en: Shen Youzhi rose in revolt; Yongzhou inspector Zhang Jinger stormed Jiangling and killed Youzhi's son Yuan Yan and his kin.
units.literal: Later Shen Youzhi rebelled; Yongzhou Inspector Zhang Jinger seized Jiangling and killed Shen Youzhi's son Yuan Yan and others.

units.zh: 永明元年元日，有小人發白虎樽，旣醉，與筆札，不知所道，直云「憶高帝」。
units.en: Yongming 1, New Year's Day: a commoner broached the White Tiger wine jar; drunk, he seized brush and paper and scrawled nonsense—over and over only "I remember the Founding Emperor."
units.literal: On New Year's Day of Yongming year 1, a petty man opened the White Tiger wine jar; drunk, he took brush and paper and wrote without knowing what—only kept saying "remembering the Founding Emperor."

units.zh: 敕原其罪。
units.en: An edict pardoned him.
units.literal: An edict pardoned his crime.

units.zh: 世祖起青溪舊宮，時人反之曰：「舊宮者，窮廄也。」
units.en: Emperor Shizu restored the old palace at Qingxi; wits reversed the name and said "Old Palace—nothing but a beggared stable."
units.literal: Emperor Shizu raised the old palace at Qingxi; people turned the name about and said "the Old Palace—that is a ruined stable."

units.zh: 及上崩後，宮人出居之。
units.en: When the emperor was gone, palace women were sent out to live there.
units.literal: After the emperor died, palace women came out to dwell there.

units.zh: 永明初，百姓歌曰：「白馬向城啼，欲得城邊草。」
units.en: Early Yongming, folk sang: "A white horse weeps at the wall, hungering for grass along the ramparts."
units.literal: Early in Yongming, the people sang: "The white horse cries toward the city, wanting the grass by the wall."

units.zh: 後句閒云「陶郎來」。
units.en: The next line ran "Young Tao is coming."
units.literal: The later line ran "Young Tao has come."

units.zh: 白者金色，馬者兵事。
units.en: White belongs to metal; the horse images war.
units.literal: White is the color of metal; horse is the image of armies.

units.zh: 三年，妖賊唐㝢之起，言唐來勞也。
units.en: In the third year the outlaw Tang Yu rebelled—his slogan that Tang had come to ease their toil.
units.literal: In year 3, the demonic bandit Tang Yu rose—his cry being that Tang comes to bring relief.

units.zh: 世祖起禪靈寺初成，百姓縱觀。
units.en: When Emperor Shizu first completed Chanling Temple, the people thronged to see it.
units.literal: When Emperor Shizu first finished the Chanling Temple, the people crowded to look.

units.zh: 或曰：「禪者授也，靈非美名，所授必不得其人。」
units.en: Some murmured: "Chan means to transmit; ling is no lucky word—whoever is handed the throne will not be fit to hold it."
units.literal: Some said: "Chan means to hand on; ling is no fair name—whoever receives the charge will surely not be the right man."

units.zh: 後太孫立，見廢也。
units.en: Soon after the heir was enthroned—and cast down.
units.literal: Later the heir apparent was set up and then deposed.

units.zh: 永明中，宮內坐起御食之外，皆爲客食。
units.en: In Yongming, inside the palace every meal but the emperor's own at morning and evening was called a guest meal.
units.literal: In Yongming, within the palace, except for the emperor's own meals at sitting and rising, all were called guest meals.

units.zh: 世祖以客非家人名，改呼爲別食，時人以爲分別之象。
units.en: Emperor Shizu said guest was no name for kin and renamed them separate meals; men read it as an omen of parting.
units.literal: Emperor Shizu held that guest was not a word for family and changed the name to separate meals; contemporaries took this as an image of separation.

units.zh: 少時，上晏駕。
units.en: Not long after, the emperor died.
units.literal: Before long the emperor died.

units.zh: 文惠太子在東宮，作「兩頭纖纖」詩，後句云「磊磊落落玉山崩」，自此長王宰相相繼薨徂，二宮晏駕。
units.en: Crown Prince Wenhui in the Eastern Palace wrote "Two Ends, Fine and Fine"; its last line was "jade mountains crumble, stone on stone"—after that great princes and chief ministers fell one after another, and both palaces buried their lords.
units.literal: Crown Prince Wenhui in the Eastern Palace composed the poem "Two Ends, Fine and Fine"; the closing line ran "jade mountains topple, heap on heap"—from then on senior princes and chief ministers died in succession, and both palaces saw the emperor die.

units.zh: 文惠太子作七言詩，後句輒云「愁和諦」。
units.en: Wenhui wrote seven-character verses whose last line always ended "sorrow—and the Harmonious Emperor."
units.literal: Crown Prince Wenhui composed seven-character poems; the closing line always ran "grief and the Emperor of Harmony."

units.zh: 後果有和帝禪位。
units.en: In time Emperor He did yield the throne.
units.literal: Later there truly was Emperor He abdicating the throne.

units.zh: 永明中，虜中童謠云：「黑水流北，赤火入齊。」
units.en: In Yongming a northern children's rhyme ran: "Black water runs northward; red fire enters Qi."
units.literal: In Yongming, among the northerners a children's rhyme said: "Black water flows north; red fire enters Qi."

units.zh: 尋而京師人家忽生火，赤於常火，熱小微，貴賤爭取以治病。
units.en: Soon fires sprang up in capital homes—brighter red than ordinary flame, barely warm; high and low scrambled to take the coals as cure.
units.literal: Soon in the capital households fire broke out without warning—redder than common flame, slight in heat; nobles and commoners vied to take it to treat illness.

units.zh: 法以此火灸桃板七炷，七日皆差。
units.en: The rite was seven burns of peachwood with that fire—within seven days every case healed.
units.literal: By the method, moxibustion with this fire on peachwood seven times cured all within seven days.

units.zh: 敕禁之，不能斷。
units.en: Edicts forbade it; nothing could stop it.
units.literal: An edict forbade it, yet could not stop it.

units.zh: 京師有病癭者，以火灸數日而差。
units.en: A man in the capital had a wen on his neck; cauterized with the fire for days, he recovered.
units.literal: In the capital someone had goiter; after several days of cautery with the fire he was cured.

units.zh: 鄰人笑曰：「病偶自差，豈火能爲。」
units.en: A neighbor scoffed: "The wen cleared on its own—what could fire have done?"
units.literal: A neighbor laughed: "The illness happened to clear by itself—how could fire do it?"

units.zh: 此人便覺頤閒癢，明日癭還如故。
units.en: At once his jaw grew itchy; next day the wen was back as before.
units.literal: The man at once felt itching at the jaw; the next day the goiter returned as before.

units.zh: 後梁以火德興。
units.en: Later Liang rose under the virtue of fire.
units.literal: Later Liang rose by the power of fire.

units.zh: 文惠太子起東田，時人反云「後必有癲童。」
units.en: Crown Prince Wenhui laid out the Eastern Fields; wits read the name backward and said "after this a frenzied child."
units.literal: Crown Prince Wenhui built the Eastern Fields; people reversed the name and said "afterward there will surely be a mad child."

units.zh: 果由太孫失位。
units.en: So it was when the heir lost his seat.
units.literal: It came about through the heir apparent losing his place.

units.zh: 齊宋以來，民間語云：「擾攘建武上。」
units.en: Since Qi and Song, folk said: "Turmoil—set Jianwu on high."
units.literal: From Qi and Song onward folk had a saying: "Turmoil—raise Jianwu above."

units.zh: 明帝初，誅害蕃戚，京師危駭。
units.en: When Emperor Ming began his reign he cut down the imperial kin; terror seized the capital.
units.literal: Early in Emperor Ming's reign he slaughtered the imperial clansmen; the capital was gripped by dread.

units.zh: 永元元年，童謠曰：「洋洋千里流，流翣東城頭。
units.en: Yongyuan 1, children sang: "Wide, wide—a thousand li runs; funeral streamers at the eastern rampart's crown.
units.literal: Yongyuan year 1, a children's rhyme: "Vast, vast—a thousand li flows; the streamer flies at the head of the eastern wall.

units.zh: 烏馬烏皮袴，三更相告訴。
units.en: Black horse, black leather breeches—at the third watch they whisper word to word.
units.literal: Black horse, black leather trousers—at the third watch they tell each other tales.

units.zh: 腳跛不得起，誤殺老姥子。」
units.en: The cripple cannot stand—by error they slay the old mother's boy."
units.literal: Lame foot cannot rise—by mistake they kill the old dame's son."

units.zh: 千里流者，江祏也。
units.en: A thousand li flows pointed to Jiang Shi.
units.literal: "A thousand li flows" was Jiang Shi.

units.zh: 東城，遙光也。
units.en: The eastern wall meant Yao Guang.
units.literal: Eastern wall—Yao Guang.

units.zh: 遙光夜舉事，垣歷生者烏皮袴褶往奔之。
units.en: Yao Guang struck by night; Yuan Lisheng ran to him in black leather breeches and jacket.
units.literal: Yao Guang rose by night; Yuan Lisheng went to join him wearing black leather trousers and jacket.

units.zh: 跛腳，亦遙光。
units.en: The cripple, too, was Yao Guang.
units.literal: Lame foot was also Yao Guang.

units.zh: 老姥子，孝字之象，徐孝嗣也。
units.en: The old mother's boy—the shape of the character for filial piety—was Xu Xiaosi.
units.literal: Old dame's son—the image of the character Xiao—was Xu Xiaosi.

units.zh: 永元中，童謠云：「野豬雖嗃嗃，馬子空閭渠。不知龍與虎，飲食江南墟。七九六十三，廣莫人無餘。烏集傳舍頭，今汝得寬休。但看三八後，摧折景陽樓。」
units.en: During Yongyuan, children sang: "Though the wild boar snorts and cries, the horse child leaves the village canal empty. Not knowing dragon and tiger, they eat and drink in the wastes south of the Yangtze. Seven times nine is sixty-three; at Guangmo no man remains. Crows gather at the relay lodge head; now you may have broad rest. Only look after three times eight: Jingyang Tower will be broken down."
units.literal: During Yongyuan, a children's rhyme said: "Though the wild boar snorts and cries, the horse child leaves the village canal empty. Not knowing dragon and tiger, they eat and drink in the wastes south of the Yangtze. Seven times nine is sixty-three; at Guangmo no man remains. Crows gather at the relay lodge head; now you may have broad rest. Only look after three times eight: Jingyang Tower will be broken down."

units.zh: 識者解云「陳顯達屬豬，崔慧景屬馬」，非也。
units.en: Those who claimed to understand it explained, "Chen Xianda belonged to the Boar, and Cui Huijing belonged to the Horse," but this was wrong.
units.literal: Those who claimed to understand it explained, "Chen Xianda belonged to the Boar, and Cui Huijing belonged to the Horse," but this was wrong.

units.zh: 東昏侯屬豬，馬子未詳，梁王屬龍，蕭穎冑屬虎。
units.en: Marquis Donghun belonged to the Boar; the horse child is unclear. The Prince of Liang belonged to the Dragon, and Xiao Yingzhou belonged to the Tiger.
units.literal: Marquis Donghun belonged to the Boar; the horse child is not clear. The Prince of Liang belonged to the Dragon, and Xiao Yingzhou belonged to the Tiger.

units.zh: 崔慧景攻臺，頓廣莫門死，時年六十三。
units.en: When Cui Huijing attacked the palace, he halted at Guangmo Gate and died; he was sixty-three at the time.
units.literal: When Cui Huijing attacked the palace, he halted at Guangmo Gate and died; he was then sixty-three years old.

units.zh: 烏集傳舍，即所謂「瞻烏爰止，于誰之屋」。
units.en: Crows gathering at the relay lodge is what is meant by, "Look at the crows, where do they stop? On whose house?"
units.literal: Crows gathering at the relay lodge is what is meant by, "Look at the crows, where do they stop? On whose house?"

units.zh: 三八二十四，起建元元年，至中興二年，二十四年也。
units.en: Three times eight is twenty-four. Counting from the first year of Jianyuan to the second year of Zhongxing gives twenty-four years.
units.literal: Three times eight is twenty-four. Counting from the first year of Jianyuan to the second year of Zhongxing gives twenty-four years.

units.zh: 摧折景陽樓，亦高臺傾之意也。
units.en: The breaking down of Jingyang Tower likewise means the overturning of the high terrace.
units.literal: Breaking down Jingyang Tower likewise means the overturning of the high terrace.

units.zh: 言天下將去，乃得休息也。
units.en: It means that when the realm was about to pass away, only then could there be rest.
units.literal: It says that once the realm was about to depart, only then could rest be obtained.

units.zh: 齊、宋之際，民間語云「和起」，言以和顏而爲變起也。
units.en: At the Qi-Song turn folk said "He rises," meaning rule would change under a mild countenance.
units.literal: At the turn of Qi and Song, folk speech said "He rises," meaning that with a gentle face change would begin.

units.zh: 後和帝立。
units.en: Later Emperor He took the throne.
units.literal: Later Emperor He was enthroned.

units.zh: 崔慧景圍臺城，有一五色幡，飛翔在雲中，半日乃不見，衆皆驚怪，相謂曰：「幡者，事尋當飜覆也。」
units.en: As Cui Huijing besieged the capital, a five-colored banner hung in the sky; half a day it would not fade; the host cried in wonder: "A banner—soon everything turns upside down."
units.literal: When Cui Huijing besieged the capital, a five-colored banner flew in the clouds; for half a day it did not vanish; the crowd was all astonished and said to one another: "A banner means affairs will soon turn over."

units.zh: 數日而慧景敗。
units.en: Within days Huijing was broken.
units.literal: Within days Huijing was defeated.

units.zh: 《言傳》曰：「言氣傷則民多口舌，故有口舌之痾。
units.en: The Treatise on Speech says: "When the breath of speech is wounded the people grow mouths upon mouths—hence sores of lip and tongue.
units.literal: The Treatise on Speech says: "When speech-air is injured the people have many mouths—hence ailments of the mouth and tongue.

units.zh: 金者白，故有日眚，若有白爲惡祥。」
units.en: Metal is white—hence blemishes on the sun; white appearing is an ill sign."
units.literal: Metal is white—hence solar afflictions; if there is white it is an evil omen."

units.zh: 宋昇明二年，飆風起建康縣南塘里，吹帛一匹入雲，風止，下御路。
units.en: Song Shengming 2: a whirlwind in Nantang hamlet, Jiankang county, lifted a bolt of cloth into the sky; when the wind died it fell on the Imperial Way.
units.literal: Song Shengming year 2, a whirlwind rose in Nantang village of Jiankang county and blew a bolt of cloth into the clouds; when the wind stopped it came down on the Imperial Way.

units.zh: 紀僧真啓太祖當宋氏禪者，其有匹夫居之。
units.en: Ji Sengzhen told Emperor Taizu that the Song mandate was his—and that a common man would dwell on the omen.
units.literal: Ji Sengzhen reported to Emperor Taizu that he would receive the Song abdication—a common man would possess it.

units.zh: 水，北方，冬藏萬物，氣至陰也，宗廟祭祀之象。
units.en: Water is the north; in winter it hoards the ten thousand things; its qi is utmost yin—the sign of ancestral rites.
units.literal: Water is the north; in winter it stores all things; its qi is utmost yin—the image of ancestral temple sacrifice.

units.zh: 死者精神放越不反，故爲之廟以收其散，爲之貌以收其魂神，而孝子得盡禮焉。
units.en: When the dead man's spirit drifts and will not come back, they raise a temple to call the scattered home and shape a likeness to call the soul home—so the filial son may offer the full rite.
units.literal: When the dead person's spirit scatters and does not return, therefore they build a temple to gather what has scattered, and make an effigy to gather soul and spirit—so that the filial son may fulfill the rites entirely.

units.zh: 敬之至，則神歆之，此則至陰之氣從，則水氣從溝瀆隨而流去，不爲民害矣。
units.en: When reverence is complete the spirits feast on it; utmost yin then aligns, and water's breath runs off through ditch and sluice without harm to the people.
units.literal: When reverence reaches the utmost the spirits savor it; then utmost-yin qi follows, and water qi follows the ditches and flows away, not harming the people.

units.zh: 人君不禱祀，簡宗廟，廢祭祀，逆天時，則霧水暴出，川水逆溢，壤邑軼鄉，沉溺民人，故曰水不潤下。
units.en: If a ruler neglects prayer and sacrifice, strips the ancestral temples, abandons the rites, and turns against the season, mist and floodwater erupt, rivers run backward and spill over, towns and hamlets are swept away, and people drown — hence the omen called water failing to soak down.
units.literal: When the ruler does not pray and sacrifice, simplifies the ancestral temples, abolishes the rites, and goes against the season, then mist-water bursts forth, rivers reverse and overflow, walled towns and villages are overrun, and the people are drowned — hence the saying that water fails to soak down.

units.zh: 建元二年，吳、吳興、義興三郡大水。
units.en: In the second year of Jianyuan, Wu, Wuxing, and Yixing commanderies were struck by great floods.
units.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan, the three commanderies of Wu, Wuxing, and Yixing suffered great floods.

units.zh: 二年夏，丹陽、吳二郡大水。
units.en: That summer, Danyang and Wu commanderies flooded.
units.literal: Year 2, summer — Danyang and Wu commanderies suffered great floods.

units.zh: 四年，大水。
units.en: Year 4 brought another great flood.
units.literal: Year 4, great flood.

units.zh: 永明五年夏，吳興、義興水雨傷稼。
units.en: Yongming 5, summer: rain and flood ruined the harvest in Wuxing and Yixing.
units.literal: Yongming year 5, summer — in Wuxing and Yixing, rain and floodwater damaged the crops.

units.zh: 六年，吳興、義興二郡大水。
units.en: Year 6: Wuxing and Yixing flooded again.
units.literal: Year 6, Wuxing and Yixing commanderies suffered great floods.

units.zh: 建武二年冬，吳、晉陵二郡水雨傷稼。
units.en: Jianwu 2, winter: rain and flood destroyed the crops in Wu and Jinling.
units.literal: Jianwu year 2, winter — in Wu and Jinling commanderies, rain and floodwater damaged the crops.

units.zh: 永元元年七月，濤入石頭，漂殺緣淮居民。
units.en: Yongyuan 1, seventh month: the tide surged into Stone Castle and swept away those living along the Huai.
units.literal: Yongyuan year 1, seventh month — the tide entered Stone Castle and drowned residents along the Huai.

units.zh: 應本傳。
units.en: It fulfilled this treatise.
units.literal: It matched this treatise.

units.zh: 荊州城內有沙池，常漏水。
units.en: Within Jingzhou city stood a sand-lined pool that never stopped leaking.
units.literal: Inside Jingzhou city was a sand pool that constantly leaked water.

units.zh: 蕭穎胄爲長史，水乃不漏，及穎胄亡，乃復竭。
units.en: While Xiao Yingzhou served as chief clerk the pool held its water; when he died, it drained away once more.
units.literal: When Xiao Yingzhou was chief clerk, the water stopped leaking; when Yingzhou died, it leaked dry again.

units.zh: 《傳》曰：「極陰氣動，故有魚孽。
units.en: The Commentary says: "When yin at its utmost begins to move, fish portents appear.
units.literal: The Commentary says: "When extreme yin qi stirs, there are fish portents.

units.zh: 魚孽者，常寒罰之符也。」
units.en: Fish portents mark the penalty of unending cold."
units.literal: Fish portents are the sign of constant cold as punishment."

units.zh: 永明九年，鹽官縣石浦有海魚乘潮來，水退不得去，長三十餘丈，黑色無鱗，未死，有聲如牛。
units.en: Yongming 9: at Shipu in Yanguan a sea fish came in on the tide and, when the water fell, could not escape — thirty-odd zhang long, black and without scales, still alive, bellowing like an ox.
units.literal: Yongming year 9, at Shipu in Yanguan county a sea fish rode the tide in; when the water receded it could not leave — more than thirty zhang long, black and scaleless, not yet dead, with a sound like an ox.

units.zh: 土人呼爲海燕，取其肉食之。
units.en: Country folk named it a "sea swallow" and butchered it for meat.
units.literal: The locals called it a "sea swallow" and ate its flesh.

units.zh: 永元元年四月，有大魚十二頭入會稽上虞江，大者近二十餘丈，小者十餘丈，一入山陰稱蒲，一入永興江，皆暍岸側，百姓取食之。
units.en: Yongyuan 1, fourth month: twelve huge fish entered the Shangyu River in Kuaiji — the largest nearly twenty zhang, the smallest above ten; one stranded at Chengpu in Shanyin, another in the Yongxing River. All lay drying on the banks while commoners carved them up for food.
units.literal: Yongyuan year 1, fourth month — twelve great fish entered the Shangyu River in Kuaiji; the largest nearly twenty-odd zhang, the smallest ten-odd zhang; one entered Chengpu in Shanyin, one the Yongxing River; all beached on the banks, and commoners ate them.

units.zh: 《聽傳》曰：「不聰之象見，則妖生於耳，以類相動，故曰有鼓妖也。」
units.en: The Listening Treatise says: "When the sign of deaf rule appears, monsters breed in the ear; like calls to like — hence the omen of the drum."
units.literal: The Listening Treatise says: "When the image of not hearing appears, portents grow in the ear; like kinds stir one another — hence there are drum portents."

units.zh: 一曰，聲屬鼓妖。
units.en: Another reading: sound itself is the drum portent.
units.literal: Another version: sound belongs to drum portents.

units.zh: 永明元年十一月癸卯夜，天東北有聲，至戊夜。
